part.text: The first annual cut shows two different signals: pedestrian injuries were lower in 2025 than 2013, while pedestrian deaths were higher. I’m charting these separately for 2013–2025; 2026 is partial, and the file has no pedestrian-exposure data to estimate risk per trip or mile walked.

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/.generate_outputs.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+query = """
+    SELECT
+        year(crash_date) AS year,
+        SUM(number_of_pedestrians_injured)::BIGINT AS pedestrian_injuries,
+        SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::BIGINT AS pedestrian_deaths
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+      AND crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+"""
+data = duckdb.sql(query).df()
+assert data["year"].tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
+
+
+def plot_metric(column, label, title, subtitle, path, annotation):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.8), layout="constrained")
+    fig.patch.set_facecolor("#f7f5f0")
+    ax.set_facecolor("#f7f5f0")
+    years = data["year"]
+    values = data[column]
+    color = "#176b87" if column == "pedestrian_injuries" else "#c23b32"
+    ax.plot(years, values, color=color, linewidth=3, marker="o", markersize=6)
+    ax.scatter([2013, 2025], [values.iloc[0], values.iloc[-1]], color=color, s=55, zorder=3)
+    ax.annotate(f"2013: {values.iloc[0]:,}", (2013, values.iloc[0]),
+                xytext=(8, 10), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=10, weight="bold")
+    ax.annotate(f"2025: {values.iloc[-1]:,}", (2025, values.iloc[-1]),
+                xytext=(-8, 10), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", fontsize=10, weight="bold")
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=19, weight="bold", pad=18, color="#17252a")
+    ax.text(0, 1.015, subtitle, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=11, color="#46545a")
+    ax.set_ylabel(label, fontsize=11)
+    ax.set_xlabel("")
+    ax.set_xticks(years)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=0, labelsize=9)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="y", labelsize=10)
+    ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#d9d7d1", linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right", "left"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color("#8b9699")
+    ax.text(0, -0.19,
+            "Source: NYC police-reported motor vehicle crash records. "
+            "Full calendar years only; counts are not adjusted for pedestrian exposure.",
+            transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, color="#46545a")
+    ax.text(0.99, 0.95, annotation, transform=ax.transAxes, ha="right", va="top",
+            fontsize=11, weight="bold", color=color,
+            bbox={"boxstyle": "round,pad=0.4", "facecolor": "white", "edgecolor": "none", "alpha": 0.85})
+    fig.savefig(path, dpi=180, facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+data[["year", "pedestrian_injuries"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+data[["year", "pedestrian_deaths"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+
+injury_change = (data.iloc[-1]["pedestrian_injuries"] / data.iloc[0]["pedestrian_injuries"] - 1) * 100
+death_change = (data.iloc[-1]["pedestrian_deaths"] / data.iloc[0]["pedestrian_deaths"] - 1) * 100
+plot_metric(
+    "pedestrian_injuries", "Pedestrians injured", "Brooklyn pedestrian injuries remain below 2013",
+    "People injured in police-reported crashes, by year", OUT / "option_1.png",
+    f"{injury_change:.0f}% vs. 2013",
+)
+plot_metric(
+    "pedestrian_deaths", "Pedestrians killed", "Brooklyn pedestrian deaths are above 2013",
+    "People killed in police-reported crashes, by year", OUT / "option_2.png",
+    f"+{death_change:.0f}% vs. 2013",
+)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians injured in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "denominator": "None; annual count",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Annual line chart",
+            "reason": "Injury counts show the annual burden of nonfatal pedestrian harm in an intuitive, locally relevant measure.",
+            "probability": 0.55,
+            "answer": f"Pedestrian injuries fell from {int(data.iloc[0]['pedestrian_injuries']):,} in 2013 to {int(data.iloc[-1]['pedestrian_injuries']):,} in 2025 ({abs(injury_change):.1f}% lower), though the count has risen each year since 2021.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether the number of pedestrians injured in Brooklyn crashes is lower than in 2013: it is, despite a steady increase since 2021. Injury counts are a defensible measure of common harm, but this chart leaves deaths and changes in the amount of walking unaccounted for; it cannot establish risk per pedestrian trip or mile.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "denominator": "None; annual count",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Annual line chart",
+            "reason": "Fatalities capture the most severe road-safety outcome and should be considered alongside injury counts.",
+            "probability": 0.45,
+            "answer": f"Pedestrian deaths increased from {int(data.iloc[0]['pedestrian_deaths'])} in 2013 to {int(data.iloc[-1]['pedestrian_deaths'])} in 2025 ({death_change:.1f}% higher), with substantial year-to-year variation.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether the most severe recorded outcome improved: pedestrian deaths were higher in 2025 than in 2013. Fatality counts are a direct measure of lethal harm, but this chart leaves nonfatal injuries and pedestrian exposure unaccounted for, so it cannot establish fatality risk per trip or mile walked.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+with (OUT / "options.json").open("w") as f:
+    json.dump(options, f, indent=2)
+    f.write("\n")
*** End Patch
